data.name: Tip_BlockUpdates
data.value: Map the Legrand firmware-update servers to 127.0.0.1 so the unit can't silently download and flash an over-the-air update that would wipe these changes. Off by default; reversible by reflashing the stock firmware.

data.name: Hint_BlockUpdates
data.value: Protects the mod from being wiped by an official update — but the unit will no longer receive updates or security fixes while blocked.

data.name: Tip_ModernHostKey
data.value: Fix two SSH host-key issues at once. (1) Adds an ECDSA host key so a modern SSH client connects without the +ssh-rsa flag — the factory dropbear only offers the SHA-1 ssh-rsa key, which OpenSSH 8.8+ rejects ("no matching host key type"). (2) Pins the RSA host key to the factory key so it stops being regenerated on every boot — no more "REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED" / ssh-keygen -R after each reboot. Off by default. The ECDSA identity is generated per build, so a rebuild + reflash of the same unit may still need a one-time ssh-keygen -R.

data.name: Hint_ModernHostKey
data.value: Fixes both "no matching host key type" (modern SSH) and the host key changing on every reboot. Ed25519 isn't used because the device's dropbear is too old for it; ECDSA works and needs no extra tooling.

data.name: Result_Build_ModernHostKey_On
data.value: SSH host keys : (ECDSA added + RSA pinned stable — modern clients, no per-boot key change)

data.name: Tip_KeepSig
data.value: Carry the original .sig signature sidecars into the rebuilt .fwz instead of dropping them. Off by default (fquinto removes them), because the signature for the modified payload becomes stale.

data.name: Hint_KeepSig
data.value: Default is to remove them (like fquinto), which is the tested path. Keeping a stale signature can make a signature-checking updater reject the archive.

data.name: Tip_MqttHaDiscovery
data.value: Publish retained MQTT discovery configs so the bridge's entities appear in Home Assistant automatically, with no manual YAML: read-only sensors (connectivity, bus dump, last key) plus control entities — a volume slider, a mute switch, volume up/down buttons, and a gate button that opens the gate. The controls send commands to the intercom over MQTT.

data.name: Hint_MqttHaDiscovery
data.value: On by default: the bridge's read-only entities (connectivity, bus, last key) and controls — a volume slider, mute, volume up/down, and a gate button — appear in Home Assistant automatically, as one device. Untick to skip it; a later build with the same device id then clears them from the broker.

data.name: Tip_MqttJson
data.value: Publish the OpenWebNet bus as one structured JSON object per frame ({frame, ts, type, who, what, where, params}) on the dump topic, instead of the raw "*...##" string. The key topic is already JSON. With Home Assistant discovery on, the bus entity exposes the parsed fields as attributes.

data.name: Hint_MqttJson
data.value: On by default: publishes structured JSON on the bus topic — easier to consume in Home Assistant and automations. Untick for raw OpenWebNet frames (low-level, dependency-free). Only the bus is affected; the key topic is already JSON.

data.name: Tip_MqttRediscovery
data.value: If the broker's IP changes on the LAN, the device finds it again — it scans the local subnet and repoints the broker name — so the bridge reconnects without a re-flash. TLS (the pinned certificate) lets it verify it reconnected to the real broker; without TLS it matches the broker's MAC address instead — captured automatically when you use Test connection on the same subnet — a convenience check for a trusted LAN, not authentication.

data.name: Hint_MqttRediscovery
data.value: On by default. Use Test connection to capture the broker's MAC so rediscovery can work without TLS on a trusted LAN (a convenience match, not authentication — use TLS for a real guarantee); entering the broker as a hostname also lets its address be repointed.

data.name: Hint_MqttDhcpReservation
data.value: Best practice: reserve the broker's IP on your router (a DHCP reservation pins it to the broker's MAC) and enter the broker as a hostname above — then its address never changes and rediscovery is only a safety net.

data.name: Fmt_MqttAnchorPinned

data.name: MqttHint_AnchorNoMac
data.value: Connected, but the broker's MAC could not be read (it may be on another subnet). Plaintext rediscovery needs a same-subnet broker; with TLS it is anchored either way.

data.name: Tip_MqttHaNodeId
data.value: Identifier for the Home Assistant device and its entities. Distinct per unit gives each bridge its own HA device; for several units on one broker, also set distinct topics (else they mirror each other). ASCII letters, digits, '_' or '-' only.

data.name: Tip_MqttLightWhere
data.value: Optional. The OpenWebNet address (WHERE) of the stair-light button on YOUR installation — the digits in the *8*21*<WHERE>## frame the panel sends when you press the light button (capture it on the bus). Leave empty to disable the Light switch. Digits only.
